clue.text: Bill is welcome? Do this to show it!

definitions.text: Bill is welcome? Do this to show it!

parts.words: Bill is welcome? Do this to show it!
parts.note: the way to show a restaurant bill is welcome is to offer to pay it for everyone at the table

explanation.surface: A cheerful instruction to demonstrate gladness at the arrival of a bill, or of a man named Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man being greeted; it is the restaurant bill, and showing it is welcome means volunteering to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to pay the whole bill, especially on behalf of a group of diners or drinkers.

clue.text: One fairly quietly spoken may be spoilt

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
mp, mezzo piano, is the musical marking for moderately quiet
aired means voiced or spoken publicly

explanation.surface: Someone who mumbles a little may be thought spoilt, a muddled bit of character judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impaired is damaged or weakened, so spoilt in its sense of harmed fits.

clue.text: Military item of clothing? Some fake piece

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asking whether a bogus bit of kit counts as military uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is a flat-topped peaked cap worn by French soldiers, an item of army headwear.

clue.text: Chaps surer to go wrong as those looking for a deal maybe

definitions.text: those looking for a deal maybe

indicators.note: letters that go wrong are knocked out of their proper order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Overconfident men may make poor bargain hunters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go wrong' rearranges CHAPS and SURER together.
explanation.definitionFit: Buyers are people who want to strike a bargain, so seekers of a deal is a loose description by example.

clue.text: Soldier is impetuous, turning up to entertain us

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold or host, so one piece sits inside another
in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: rash means acting hastily or impetuously

explanation.surface: A soldier who is hot-headed and comes round to amuse the speaker's group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' applies because this is a down entry: the word for impetuous is read bottom to top, then 'to entertain' takes US in.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a cavalry soldier, originally a Hungarian light horseman.

clue.text: Excessively keen initially, excellent leader of men prepared to shoot

parts.note: too means excessively

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate or excellent

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A very keen, outstanding officer readies his troops to fire.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a common way of saying excellent, entered here as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: To take aim is to point a weapon at a target, getting ready to fire it.

clue.text: Amazing function of device used by suspicious police

definitions.text: function of device used by suspicious police
definitions.meaning: a breathalyser's job is literally the taking of a driver's breath sample

explanation.surface: An amazing function of a gadget police use when they suspect something.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into BREATH TAKING: police who suspect drink-driving take a breath sample with a breathalyser.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that takes your breath away is astonishing, and the literal reading names what a breath test does.

clue.text: Yesteryear's class meeting important lady

definitions.note: an adjective-like possessive, matching the adjective sense of the answer

parts.note: a form is a school class
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: An old school class reunion with a distinguished woman attending.
explanation.definitionFit: Former means belonging to an earlier time, just as yesteryear's describes things of the past.

clue.text: Work at back of company in small enclosure

indicators.note: at back of places the first piece after the second

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone working behind a firm's premises in a small pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A coop is a small cage or pen, especially one for keeping chickens.

clue.text: What may help little person to see fairy's garment

definitions.text: What may help little person to see

parts.note: a peri is a fairy of Persian myth, so fairy's gives PERI'S
a cope is a long cloak worn by priests

explanation.surface: A short person wants to see a fairy's dress.
explanation.walkthrough: A short person in a crowd can see over heads with a periscope.
explanation.definitionFit: A periscope lets someone view over obstacles, so it helps a short spectator see.

clue.text: Pianists ignoring the bass clef?

parts.note: the bass clef part is played by the left hand, so pianists ignoring it use only the other hand

explanation.surface: Pianists who disregard the lower stave of the music.
explanation.walkthrough: In piano music the bass clef stave is for the left hand; drop it and only the treble, right-hand part remains.
explanation.definitionFit: People who favour their right hand are punningly pictured as pianists playing only the treble part.

clue.text: Like some verse coming from this writer's biro?

parts.note: this writer is the setter, so this writer's, read as this writer is, gives I AM
Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, like a Biro

explanation.surface: Poetry flowing from the setter's ballpoint pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer's' is read as 'this writer is', I AM. Biro is the British everyday name for a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambic verse is built from iambs, a metre used in much English poetry.

clue.text: Bird hard for country person to bag

indicators.note: to bag is to put in a bag, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a peasant is a rural worker
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A game bird that a countryman finds difficult to shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bag' also suggests shooting game, but here it puts H inside PEASANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The pheasant is a long-tailed game bird.

clue.text: Ungodly and faint-hearted person is buried in barren land

indicators.note: being buried in something means lying inside it

parts.note: a heath is open uncultivated land
a hen, like a chicken, is slang for a coward
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cowardly, godless man lies buried on a bleak moor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is buried in' places the timid bird and IS within the moorland word, before its final letter. A hen, like a chicken, stands for a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathenish means like a heathen, irreligious or pagan.

clue.text: 'Common' Arabs maybe seen wandering about

parts.note: Arabs are a breed of horse, so these are an example

indicators.note: letters wandering about move out of place and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arab horses spotted roaming over a common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' in quotes stands for common sense; 'wandering about' rearranges SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse sense is plain practical wisdom, otherwise called common sense.

clue.text: Issue of the day, say, being gone over

indicators.note: gone over suggests turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the day is an example of time

explanation.surface: A matter of current debate being reviewed.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to give out or send forth, as a chimney emits smoke.

clue.text: More peculiar person children are taught to avoid?

definitions.meaning: odder, the comparative of an adjective meaning weird

definitions.text: person children are taught to avoid?
definitions.meaning: children are warned against talking to people they do not know

explanation.surface: An odder figure is the one youngsters learn to steer clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative means odder, and the noun is someone unknown, warned against in stranger danger.

clue.text: State of irritation? Blow!

definitions.meaning: a sulk or fit of pique
to puff or exhale, as the wolf did to blow the house down

explanation.surface: An exasperated exclamation from someone in a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: One being in a fit of pique, the other meaning to puff out air.

clue.text: Anger in agricultural business — one gets fired

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: a farm is an agricultural business
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Rage on a farm ends with a worker being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets fired' suggests dismissal, but a gun is what gets fired.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun is discharged, so it is the thing that is fired.

clue.text: Celebrity's vehicle makes one deeply impressed

parts.note: a celebrity is a star, so celebrity's gives STAR'S
a truck is a goods vehicle

explanation.surface: A famous person's car leaves a fan in awe.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dazzled by fame or celebrity makes one overawed, deeply impressed.

clue.text: One person supervising journalists in team?

parts.note: a unit is one
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A single editor working within a group.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: many British football teams are called United, such as Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: United is a common name for a football side, so it is an example of a team.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about a vehicle seen in the capital

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece sits round another

parts.note: ha is an exclamation of surprise
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at a car spotted in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Havana is the capital of Cuba.

clue.text: A ranter's ridiculous reports

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests something absurdly out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loudmouth's absurd news accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell or relate a story, so it reports events.

clue.text: Hostile African country with guns regularly seen

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hostile African state where armed men are a common sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Malign means evil-intentioned or hostile, as in a malign influence.

clue.text: Aims to finish before start of supper

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: end means finish

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Goals of wrapping things up before the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends are goals or purposes, as in ends and means.

clue.text: What comes out from English master meeting people

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: An English schoolmaster addressing the populace.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something given off or issuing from a source, like a vapour.

clue.text: Someone leaving is energetic type

explanation.surface: A departing person is a lively sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one who goes, and colloquially a lively, active person or thing.

clue.text: Helpful folk reforming parish system

indicators.note: reforming means forming again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kind people overhauling how a parish is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters who share and back a cause are kindly, supportive people.
